symptom: PC1 cannot reach Server1 in VLAN 30.
topology_note: Router-on-a-stick with sub-interfaces for VLAN 10 and VLAN 30 on GigabitEthernet0/0.
show_outputs:
GigabitEthernet0/0.10 is up, line protocol is up
GigabitEthernet0/0.30 is administratively down, line protocol is down
expected_fault: VLAN 30 router sub-interface is administratively down.
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | interface GigabitEthernet0/0.30 | no shutdown

symptom: Hosts on VLAN 20 cannot reach hosts on VLAN 10, but both VLANs work locally.
topology_note: Switch trunk to router configured; router has sub-interfaces for VLAN 10 and VLAN 20.
show_outputs:
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.20
 encapsulation dot1Q 20
 ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.10
 encapsulation dot1Q 10
 ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0
GigabitEthernet0/0.20 is up, line protocol is up
expected_fault: Inter-VLAN routing sub-interfaces appear correctly configured; likely an access-list or missing route is blocking inter-VLAN traffic rather than VLAN config itself.
expected_fix_steps: Verify routing table contains both VLAN subnets | Check for access-lists applied to sub-interfaces | Remove or correct blocking ACL

symptom: New PC connected to switch port Fa0/5 cannot get an IP address and is isolated from the rest of VLAN 30.
topology_note: Access switch with VLAN 30 assigned to most ports.
show_outputs:
interface FastEthernet0/5
 switchport mode access
 switchport access vlan 99
FastEthernet0/5 is up, line protocol is up
expected_fault: Port Fa0/5 is assigned to VLAN 99 instead of VLAN 30 (missing/incorrect VLAN assignment).
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | interface FastEthernet0/5 | switchport access vlan 30

symptom: Trunk link between SW1 and SW2 is not passing VLAN 40 traffic even though both switches have VLAN 40 defined.
topology_note: Trunk configured between SW1 Gi0/1 and SW2 Gi0/1.
show_outputs:
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 switchport mode trunk
 switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,30
GigabitEthernet0/1 is up, line protocol is up
expected_fault: VLAN 40 is not included in the trunk's allowed VLAN list (trunk pruning misconfiguration).
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | interface GigabitEthernet0/1 | switchport trunk allowed vlan add 40

symptom: PC3 on SW2 cannot communicate with PC4 on SW1, although both are supposedly in VLAN 20.
topology_note: Two access switches connected via a trunk link; VLAN 20 exists on SW1 but was never created on SW2.
show_outputs:
SW2#show vlan brief
VLAN Name Status Ports
1 default active Fa0/1, Fa0/2
(VLAN 20 not listed)
expected_fault: VLAN 20 does not exist in the VLAN database on SW2 (VLAN mismatch between switches).
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | vlan 20 | name USERS | exit | interface FastEthernet0/2 | switchport access vlan 20

symptom: PC on LAN A cannot reach the server on LAN B across two routers, though both LAN interfaces are up.
topology_note: R1 and R2 connected via a serial link; static routing environment.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip route
C 192.168.1.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
C 10.0.0.0/30 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0
(no route to 192.168.2.0/24)
expected_fault: R1 is missing a static or dynamic route to the remote LAN B network (192.168.2.0/24).
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | ip route 192.168.2.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.2

symptom: OSPF neighbors between R1 and R2 are not forming; routing table on R1 has no OSPF routes.
topology_note: R1 and R2 connected via Serial0/0/0, OSPF area 0 configured on both.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip ospf neighbor
(no output - no neighbors found)
R1#show run | include network
network 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 area 0
expected_fault: The serial link network statement for OSPF is missing on R1, so OSPF cannot form a neighbor relationship over the WAN link.
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | router ospf 1 | network 10.0.0.0 0.0.0.3 area 0

symptom: Branch router can ping its directly connected networks but cannot reach the HQ network across the WAN.
topology_note: Branch router uses a default static route pointing to the wrong next-hop IP.
show_outputs:
Branch#show ip route
S* 0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 172.16.0.254
C 172.16.0.0/30 is directly connected, Serial0/0/0
expected_fault: The default route's next-hop IP (172.16.0.254) does not match the HQ-side interface address, so the default route is unreachable/incorrect.

symptom: Some remote subnets are unreachable after adding a new router to the topology; routing table shows fewer routes than expected.
topology_note: EIGRP running between three routers; new router R3 was just added.
show_outputs:
R3#show ip eigrp neighbors
(no neighbors)
R3#show run | include autonomous-system
router eigrp 10
expected_fault: R3 is missing the required 'network' statements under EIGRP, so it has not formed adjacencies and is not advertising or learning routes.
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | router eigrp 10 | network 192.168.3.0 0.0.0.255 | network 10.0.0.4 0.0.0.3

symptom: Traffic destined for the internet works, but traffic to a specific internal subnet (192.168.5.0/24) times out.
topology_note: Router has a default route to the ISP and several static internal routes.
expected_fault: A static route for the 192.168.5.0/24 subnet is missing, so traffic to that internal network is unreachable and falls through unexpectedly or is dropped.
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | ip route 192.168.5.0 255.255.255.0 10.0.0.2

symptom: PCs in VLAN 10 are not receiving IP addresses automatically and show APIPA addresses (169.254.x.x).
topology_note: Router configured as DHCP server for VLAN 10 pool.
show_outputs:
R1#show run | section dhcp
ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.10.1 192.168.10.10
(no ip dhcp pool VLAN10 found)
expected_fault: The DHCP pool for VLAN 10 has not been created on the router, so no addresses are being offered.
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | ip dhcp pool VLAN10 | network 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0 | default-router 192.168.10.1 | dns-server 8.8.8.8

symptom: Only some PCs in VLAN 20 receive IP addresses; others get APIPA addresses intermittently.
topology_note: DHCP pool exists but the address range is nearly exhausted.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip dhcp pool VLAN20
Pool VLAN20 :
 Total addresses : 20
 Leased addresses : 20
 Excluded addresses : 5
expected_fault: The DHCP scope for VLAN 20 is exhausted (all leasable addresses are in use), so new clients cannot obtain a lease.
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | ip dhcp pool VLAN20 | network 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0 (expand the subnet or clear stale leases with clear ip dhcp binding *)

symptom: PCs on a remote VLAN across a router cannot get DHCP addresses from the central DHCP server, though local VLAN clients can.
topology_note: DHCP server is centralized on R1; VLAN 30 is on a different router-connected segment reached via a relay.
show_outputs:
R2#show run interface g0/0.30
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.30
 encapsulation dot1Q 30
 ip address 192.168.30.1 255.255.255.0
(no ip helper-address configured)
expected_fault: The 'ip helper-address' command is missing on the VLAN 30 sub-interface, so DHCP broadcast requests are not relayed to the central DHCP server.
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | interface GigabitEthernet0/0.30 | ip helper-address 192.168.10.1

symptom: A PC in VLAN 10 receives an IP address from the wrong subnet (192.168.99.x instead of 192.168.10.x).
topology_note: Two DHCP pools exist on the router; the VLAN10 pool has a misconfigured network statement.
show_outputs:
R1#show run | section dhcp pool VLAN10
ip dhcp pool VLAN10
 network 192.168.99.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 192.168.10.1
expected_fault: The DHCP pool named VLAN10 is bound to the wrong network (192.168.99.0) instead of 192.168.10.0.
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | ip dhcp pool VLAN10 | network 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0

symptom: PCs can ping the web server by IP address but cannot browse to it by hostname.
topology_note: DHCP pool does not specify a DNS server option.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip dhcp pool VLAN10
 network 192.168.10.0 255.255.255.0
 default-router 192.168.10.1
(no dns-server line present)
expected_fault: The DHCP pool does not advertise a DNS server, so clients cannot resolve hostnames despite having IP-layer connectivity.
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | ip dhcp pool VLAN10 | dns-server 8.8.8.8

symptom: All name resolution fails network-wide; PCs report 'DNS request timed out' for every domain.
topology_note: Static DNS server IP configured on PCs points to an address that does not exist on the network.
show_outputs:
PC1> ipconfig /all
DNS Servers: 192.168.10.250
R1#show ip route
(192.168.10.250 is not reachable; no host at that address)
expected_fault: The configured DNS server address (192.168.10.250) does not correspond to any real DNS server on the network.
expected_fix_steps: Verify correct DNS server address with instructor/topology documentation | Update DHCP pool or PC static DNS setting to the correct DNS server IP

symptom: Internal hostnames resolve fine, but external domains (e.g. an internet-style test domain) fail to resolve.
topology_note: Local DNS server is configured to forward unresolved external queries, but forwarding is not configured.
show_outputs:
DNS-Server#show run | include forward
(no dns forwarder configured)
expected_fault: The DNS server is not configured to forward queries it cannot resolve locally, so external/unknown domains fail.
expected_fix_steps: Configure a forwarding/upstream DNS server on the local DNS service | Re-test external name resolution

symptom: PC1 in VLAN 10 cannot reach the server in VLAN 30, but ping to the router's own interfaces succeeds.
topology_note: An extended ACL is applied inbound on the VLAN 10 sub-interface.
show_outputs:
R1#show access-lists
Extended IP access list 101
 10 deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 192.168.30.0 0.0.0.255 (25 matches)
 20 permit ip any any
expected_fault: Access-list 101 explicitly denies traffic from VLAN 10 to VLAN 30 before the permit-any statement is reached.
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | no access-list 101 deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 192.168.30.0 0.0.0.255 (or add a specific permit statement above the deny, matching intended policy)

symptom: Telnet access to R2 from the admin PC is being refused even though the password is correct.
topology_note: VTY lines reference access-class 10 restricting management access.
show_outputs:
R2#show run | section line vty
line vty 0 4
 access-class 10 in
 password cisco
 login
R2#show access-lists 10
Standard IP access list 10
 10 permit 192.168.99.5
expected_fault: Access-list 10 on the VTY lines only permits a different management host (192.168.99.5), so the admin PC's address is not allowed to Telnet in.
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | access-list 10 permit <admin PC IP address> | end

symptom: Web traffic (HTTP) to the server works, but FTP to the same server is blocked for all users.
topology_note: Extended ACL applied on the server-facing interface filters by port/protocol.
show_outputs:
R1#show access-lists 120
Extended IP access list 120
 10 permit tcp any host 192.168.30.10 eq 80
 20 deny tcp any host 192.168.30.10 eq 21
 30 permit ip any any
expected_fault: ACL 120 explicitly denies TCP port 21 (FTP control) to the server while permitting port 80 (HTTP).
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | no 20 (remove the deny line inside ACL 120 if numbered, or recreate the ACL) | access-list 120 permit tcp any host 192.168.30.10 eq 21

symptom: After applying a new security ACL, all traffic through the router stopped, including traffic that should be allowed.
topology_note: New extended ACL was applied to an interface without a final explicit permit statement.
show_outputs:
R1#show access-lists 150
Extended IP access list 150
 10 deny tcp any any eq 23
(implicit deny any any at end of list)
expected_fault: ACL 150 has no explicit permit statements, so the implicit 'deny any any' at the end of the ACL blocks all traffic, not just Telnet.
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | access-list 150 permit ip any any | (place this after the specific deny statements, then re-apply/verify the ACL)

symptom: Internal PCs cannot reach the internet-simulated network even though the default route is correct.
topology_note: Router configured for PAT (NAT overload) toward the outside interface.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip nat translations
(no translations present)
R1#show run | include ip nat
ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 overload
(GigabitEthernet0/0 missing 'ip nat inside')
expected_fault: The internal-facing interface (GigabitEthernet0/0) is missing the 'ip nat inside' command, so NAT is not applied to internal traffic.
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | interface GigabitEthernet0/0 | ip nat inside | interface GigabitEthernet0/1 | ip nat outside

symptom: Internal hosts can reach the outside network, but an externally-hosted test server cannot initiate connections to the internal web server via the public IP.
topology_note: Static NAT/port-forwarding rule is intended for the internal web server on port 80.
show_outputs:
R1#show run | include ip nat
ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 overload
(no static NAT entry for internal web server present)
expected_fault: There is no static (or port-forwarding) NAT entry for the internal web server, so inbound connections from outside cannot reach it — only outbound PAT is configured.
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | ip nat inside source static tcp 192.168.10.10 80 <public IP> 80

symptom: NAT overload is configured, but internal PCs still cannot reach the outside network; translation table stays empty.
topology_note: NAT pool/ACL used to define which internal traffic gets translated.
show_outputs:
R1#show access-lists 1
(access-list 1 not found)
R1#show run | include ip nat inside source
ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/1 overload
expected_fault: Access-list 1, which is supposed to define the internal traffic eligible for NAT, does not exist, so nothing is being translated.
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | access-list 1 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255

symptom: PC1 can ping other devices in its own subnet but cannot reach any device outside its subnet.
topology_note: PC1 configured manually with a static IP.
show_outputs:
PC1> ipconfig
IP Address: 192.168.10.25
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.0
Default Gateway: 192.168.10.100
expected_fault: PC1's configured default gateway (192.168.10.100) does not match the router's actual interface address on that subnet (typically 192.168.10.1), so off-subnet traffic has no valid next hop.
expected_fix_steps: On PC1, update the default gateway to match the router's LAN interface IP address (e.g. 192.168.10.1) | Retest connectivity to a remote subnet

symptom: Two PCs in the same physical VLAN and switch cannot ping each other, and both report intermittent connectivity issues.
topology_note: PCs statically configured, IP addressing assigned manually by students.
show_outputs:
PC1> ipconfig
IP Address: 192.168.10.25
PC2> ipconfig
IP Address: 192.168.10.25
expected_fault: Duplicate IP address (192.168.10.25) has been assigned to both PC1 and PC2, causing intermittent connectivity and ARP conflicts.
expected_fix_steps: Assign PC2 a unique IP address within the subnet (e.g. 192.168.10.26) | Clear ARP caches and retest connectivity

symptom: PC1 can reach some hosts in what should be its own subnet but not others, and subnet math seems inconsistent.
topology_note: PC1 was configured with a subnet mask narrower than the rest of the VLAN.
show_outputs:
PC1> ipconfig
IP Address: 192.168.10.50
Subnet Mask: 255.255.255.128
Other hosts on VLAN use: 255.255.255.0
expected_fault: PC1 has an incorrect subnet mask (255.255.255.128) that splits the VLAN into two logical subnets, so it cannot reach hosts in the other half of the /24.
expected_fix_steps: On PC1, correct the subnet mask to 255.255.255.0 to match the rest of the VLAN | Retest connectivity to previously unreachable hosts

symptom: Laptop cannot see the classroom wireless network (SSID) in its available networks list.
topology_note: Wireless router/AP configured with SSID broadcast disabled for a lab exercise.
show_outputs:
AP-Config#show run | include ssid
ssid Classroom-WiFi
(broadcast-ssid disabled)
expected_fault: SSID broadcast is disabled on the access point, so the network does not appear in the client's scan list even though it is otherwise reachable.
expected_fix_steps: On the AP, enable SSID broadcast, or manually enter the exact SSID name on the client device | Retest network visibility

symptom: Laptop can see and select the wireless SSID but repeatedly fails to authenticate.
topology_note: WPA2-PSK configured on the AP; students may have a typo in the passphrase.
show_outputs:
AP-Config#show run | include auth
authentication wpa2-psk
passphrase C1sc0Lab2024
expected_fault: The wireless client is likely using an incorrect passphrase, causing repeated WPA2-PSK authentication failures.
expected_next_command: show wireless client status (or review AP authentication logs)
expected_fix_steps: Re-enter the correct WPA2 passphrase on the client device | Confirm the AP passphrase matches the documented lab credential

symptom: Two wireless clients associated with the same AP cannot ping each other, though both reach the wired network fine.
topology_note: AP configured with client (peer-to-peer) isolation enabled for security.
show_outputs:
AP-Config#show run | include isolation
wireless client-isolation enabled
expected_fault: Wireless client isolation is enabled on the AP, intentionally blocking direct traffic between wireless clients while still allowing access to the wired network.
expected_fix_steps: If peer-to-peer wireless communication is required, disable client isolation on the AP | Otherwise, document this as expected/by-design security behavior

symptom: PC1 cannot reach the router's own gateway interface, and the switch port LED for that PC is off.
topology_note: Physical/logical interface state issue directly on the access switch port.
show_outputs:
SW1#show interfaces FastEthernet0/3 status
Port Name Status Vlan Duplex Speed Type
Fa0/3 notconnect 10 auto auto 10/100BaseTX
Fa0/3 is down, line protocol is down (notconnect)
expected_fault: The switch port FastEthernet0/3 is down (notconnect), indicating a physical link problem such as a bad cable or the device being powered off.
expected_fix_steps: Verify the physical cable connection and that the end device is powered on | Reseat or replace the cable | Verify the port is not administratively disabled

symptom: PC1 in VLAN 10 cannot reach Server1 in VLAN 30, but VLAN 20 to VLAN 30 works fine.
topology_note: Router-on-a-stick; VLAN 10 sub-interface uses a different encapsulation VLAN ID than the switch trunk expects.
show_outputs:
R1#show run interface g0/0.10
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.10
 encapsulation dot1Q 15
 ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0
expected_fault: The router sub-interface for VLAN 10 is configured with the wrong dot1Q tag (15 instead of 10), causing a VLAN ID mismatch with the switch trunk.
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | interface GigabitEthernet0/0.10 | encapsulation dot1Q 10

symptom: After a topology change, PC1 can reach the local router but no other remote networks are reachable, and the routing table appears mostly empty.
topology_note: Dynamic routing protocol was recently removed/reconfigured and static backup routes were never added.
show_outputs:
R1#show ip route
C 192.168.1.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
(no other routes present)
expected_fault: All remote routes are missing from the routing table; the router has only directly connected networks, indicating a missing routing protocol/static route configuration.
expected_fix_steps: Verify intended routing method (static vs dynamic) with topology documentation | Reconfigure the routing protocol or add the required static routes

symptom: PC1 gets an IP address successfully but cannot ping its own default gateway.
topology_note: DHCP-assigned default gateway option does not match the router's actual interface IP.
show_outputs:
PC1> ipconfig
Default Gateway: 192.168.10.254
R1#show ip interface brief
GigabitEthernet0/0 192.168.10.1 up up
expected_fault: The DHCP-assigned default gateway (192.168.10.254) does not match the router's actual LAN interface address (192.168.10.1).
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | ip dhcp pool VLAN10 | default-router 192.168.10.1

symptom: Traffic from VLAN 10 to VLAN 30 is denied by the firewall/ACL, but the case owner insists the ACL was already removed.
topology_note: An old ACL is still applied to the interface even though its contents were cleared.
show_outputs:
R1#show run interface g0/0.10
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.10
 ip access-group 101 in
R1#show access-lists 101
(access-list 101 has no entries — treated as empty/undefined)
expected_fault: An access-group reference to ACL 101 is still applied to the interface even though the ACL itself is empty/removed, which can cause unpredictable behavior depending on IOS version.
expected_fix_steps: configure terminal | interface GigabitEthernet0/0.10 | no ip access-group 101 in
